title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ecclesiastes chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ecclesiastes Chapter 9.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:1, who are in the hand of God?
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous and the wise
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:1 states that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:2 says there is a different event for the righteous and the wicked.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:2 explains that all things come alike to all; there is one event to the righteous and to the wicked.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:3 say is full of evil?
options: The heart of the sons of men
questions.correctAnswer: The heart of the sons of men
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:3 states that the heart of the sons of men is full of evil.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:4, which is better: a living dog or a dead lion?
questions.correctAnswer: A living dog
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:4 says a living dog is better than a dead lion.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:5 says the dead know everything and receive rewards.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:5 states the dead know nothing and have no more reward.

questions.question: What has perished according to Ecclesiastes 9:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Love, hatred, and envy
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:6 says that love, hatred, and envy have perished for the dead.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:7, what should one do with their bread and wine?
options: Eat with joy and drink with a merry heart
questions.correctAnswer: Eat with joy and drink with a merry heart
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:7 commands to eat bread with joy and drink wine with a merry heart.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:8 advises that one's garments should always be white.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:8 instructs to let thy garments be always white.

questions.question: In Ecclesiastes 9:9, with whom should one live joyfully?
options: With the wife whom thou lovest
questions.correctAnswer: With the wife whom thou lovest
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:9 says to live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of life.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:10, what should one do with whatsoever their hand findeth to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Do it with thy might
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:10 commands to do whatsoever thy hand findeth to do with thy might.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Ecclesiastes 9:11 as something that gives advantage in the race of life?
questions.correctAnswer: Being wealthy
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:11 mentions that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise; riches are also mentioned but the verse says time and chance happen to all, showing no advantage.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:12 compares men to fishes and birds caught unexpectedly.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:12 compares men to fishes taken in a net and birds caught in a snare.

questions.question: What did the poor wise man do in the little city in Ecclesiastes 9:15?
options: Delivered the city by his wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Delivered the city by his wisdom
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:15 says the poor wise man delivered the city by his wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:16, wisdom is considered better than what?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:16 states that wisdom is better than strength.

questions.question: What is said to be better than weapons of war in Ecclesiastes 9:18?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:18 says wisdom is better than weapons of war.

medium.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:7, what should one do with their bread and wine?
options: Eat with sorrow and drink with fear
Eat with joy and drink with a merry heart
Fast and pray before eating or drinking
questions.correctAnswer: Eat with joy and drink with a merry heart
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:7 instructs to 'eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart' because God accepts the works done. This promotes a joyful and thankful attitude in daily living, supported by verses 7 and 9 which emphasize joy and enjoying life.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:8 advise about one's appearance and self-care?
options: Wear dark clothes and avoid perfumes
Let garments be always white and let the head lack no ointment
Wear simple clothes and refrain from anointing
questions.correctAnswer: Let garments be always white and let the head lack no ointment
questions.explanation: Verse 8 encourages maintaining purity and enjoyment of life symbolized by white garments and anointing the head, indicating a celebration of life and vitality in the midst of vanity, linking with joyfulness in verse 9.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 9:9 suggest one should live with their spouse?
options: With patience and tolerance for all days
Joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy life
questions.correctAnswer: Joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy life
questions.explanation: Verse 9 encourages joyful living with the spouse throughout life's fleeting days, emphasizing love and enjoyment as one's portion under the sun, which complements the joyful themes in verses 7 and 8.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:10, how should one approach their work?
options: Do it with might and full effort
Delay it until the right moment
questions.correctAnswer: Do it with might and full effort
questions.explanation: Verse 10 teaches that whatever work one finds to do, it should be done with full strength because there is no work or wisdom in the grave, highlighting the urgency and value of diligent effort in life.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:11 reveal about the outcomes of life's races and battles?
options: The swift always win the race
The strong always win the battle
Time and chance happen to all, regardless of strength or wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Time and chance happen to all, regardless of strength or wisdom
questions.explanation: Verse 11 shows that success is not guaranteed by natural abilities or wisdom alone but that time and chance affect everyone, teaching humility and trust in God's sovereignty.

questions.question: What practical truth about time and human knowledge is taught in Ecclesiastes 9:12?
options: Man knows exactly when his time will come
Time is controlled by human plans
Man does not know his time and is caught unexpectedly like fish in a net
Only the wise can avoid sudden evil times
questions.correctAnswer: Man does not know his time and is caught unexpectedly like fish in a net
questions.explanation: Verse 12 uses imagery of fish and birds caught unexpectedly to illustrate that humans cannot know their appointed time, encouraging vigilance and reliance on God’s timing.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 9:7 connect with verse 10 in terms of living and working?
options: Verse 7's joy contrasts with verse 10's warning about laziness
Verse 7 encourages joy in life while verse 10 commands doing work with might, emphasizing enjoyment and diligence in life
Verse 7 focuses on prayer, verse 10 on fasting
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 7 encourages joy in life while verse 10 commands doing work with might, emphasizing enjoyment and diligence in life
questions.explanation: Verse 7 advises joyful enjoyment of life’s blessings while verse 10 urges wholehearted effort in work, together teaching a balanced Christian life of joy and diligence under God’s acceptance.

questions.question: Based on Ecclesiastes 9:9 and 10, what biblical truth applies to a believer struggling to find purpose in daily tasks?
options: Life is meaningless and work pointless
Enjoy life with loved ones and put full effort into your work because there is no work after death
Avoid work and focus on spiritual matters only
Wait passively for purpose to come
questions.correctAnswer: Enjoy life with loved ones and put full effort into your work because there is no work after death
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 teach to live joyfully with loved ones and work diligently since life is temporary and there is no work after death, encouraging purposeful living and commitment.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:11 teach about the fairness of life’s outcomes?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 11 states that the race is not always won by the swift nor the battle by the strong, showing that life’s outcomes are not always fair or according to human expectations, but subject to time and chance.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:12 says that people can predict the time of their death.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Verse 12 clearly states that man does not know his time, comparing humans to fish and birds caught unexpectedly, emphasizing unpredictability rather than predictability.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:13, the wisdom seen under the sun seemed what?
questions.correctAnswer: Great and impressive
questions.explanation: Verse 13 states 'This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me,' indicating the author's recognition of the value and impressiveness of practical wisdom.

questions.question: What lesson does the story in Ecclesiastes 9:14-15 teach about wisdom and recognition?
options: Wisdom can save, but the wise might be forgotten or unappreciated
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom can save, but the wise might be forgotten or unappreciated
questions.explanation: Verses 14-15 describe a poor wise man who delivered the city yet was not remembered, teaching that wisdom is valuable though often unrecognized by society.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:16 say about the value of wisdom versus strength?
options: Strength is always better than wisdom
Wisdom is better than strength, but often despised if from the poor
Only strength can save a city
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is better than strength, but often despised if from the poor
questions.explanation: Verse 16 asserts that wisdom surpasses strength, yet the wisdom of the poor is often ignored or despised, highlighting social attitudes toward wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:17, whose words are more effective than the cries of rulers among fools?
questions.correctAnswer: Wise men in quiet
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states that the words of wise men heard in quiet are more effective than the loud cries of foolish rulers, emphasizing the power of calm wisdom over noisy folly.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:18 teaches that one sinner can destroy much good, even though wisdom is better than weapons of war.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Verse 18 contrasts wisdom as better than weapons of war but warns that one sinner can cause great destruction, underscoring the impact of sin despite wisdom's value.

hard.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ecclesiastes Chapter 9.

questions.question: What did the author observe about wisdom under the sun in Ecclesiastes 9:13?
questions.correctAnswer: It seemed great unto him
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:13 states that the wisdom observed under the sun seemed great to the author, highlighting its apparent value.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:14, what was the condition of the city before the siege?
options: It was a little city with few men
It was a large city with many men
It was a wealthy trading hub
questions.correctAnswer: It was a little city with few men
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes a little city with few men within it that was besieged by a great king, emphasizing its small size and vulnerability.

questions.question: Who saved the city by wisdom in Ecclesiastes 9:15?
questions.correctAnswer: A poor wise man
questions.explanation: The verse notes that a poor wise man delivered the city by his wisdom, though he was not remembered, illustrating the theme of unnoticed wisdom.

questions.question: What conclusion does the author draw about wisdom versus strength in Ecclesiastes 9:16?
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is better than strength
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:16 explicitly states that wisdom is better than strength, though the poor man's wisdom is often despised.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:17 say about how the words of wise men are received compared to the cries of fools?
options: Words of wise men are heard more in quiet
Cries of fools are more respected
Fools' cries are heard in quiet
questions.correctAnswer: Words of wise men are heard more in quiet
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the calm reception of wise men's words with the disruptive cries of fools, emphasizing the power of quiet wisdom.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:18, what is wisdom compared to, and what can a sinner do?
options: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good
Wisdom is equal to weapons of war, and sinners do little harm
Weapons of war are better than wisdom, and sinners are powerless
Wisdom is unrelated to war, and sinners build good
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner destroys much good
questions.explanation: The verse clearly compares wisdom favorably against weapons of war but warns that a single sinner can ruin much good, a theme echoed in Proverbs 10:12.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme that time and chance affect all, as described in Ecclesiastes 9:11?
questions.correctAnswer: Proverbs 16:33
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:11 teaches that time and chance happen to all, a concept echoed in Proverbs 16:33, which states that the lot is cast into the lap, but the whole disposing thereof is of the Lord.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:12 use as a metaphor for men being caught unexpectedly?
options: Fishes taken in a net and birds caught in a snare
Lions trapped in a hunter’s den
questions.correctAnswer: Fishes taken in a net and birds caught in a snare
questions.explanation: Verse 12 uses the imagery of fishes taken in an evil net and birds caught in a snare to illustrate how men are snared suddenly and unexpectedly by evil times.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave' in Ecclesiastes 9:10 imply about life and death?
options: One must do their work with might while alive
Wisdom is eternal beyond the grave
questions.correctAnswer: One must do their work with might while alive
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:10 exhorts doing all work with might because in the grave, there is no work, device, knowledge, or wisdom, emphasizing the finality of death.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 9:9 instruct one to live with their wife?
options: Live joyfully with her all the days of thy vanity
questions.correctAnswer: Live joyfully with her all the days of thy vanity
questions.explanation: The verse encourages joyfully living with the wife one loves during the fleeting days of life, recognizing this as a portion given by God under the sun.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:7 say about how one should accept their work?
options: Ignore the results of your work
questions.correctAnswer: God now accepteth thy works
questions.explanation: Verse 7 encourages eating, drinking, and enjoying life because God now accepts the works of the individual, emphasizing divine acceptance over human.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Ecclesiastes 9:11 to convey the unpredictability of life?
options: Chiasm focusing on strength and wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism illustrating contrasts
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:11 uses parallelism by contrasting swift, strong, wise, rich, and skillful men with the reality that time and chance happen to all, showing life’s unpredictability.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word 'wisdom' (חָכְמָה, chokmah) as used in Ecclesiastes 9:16, and how does it relate to the verse’s message?
options: Skill in living and practical insight, showing its superiority to strength
Wealth and power, highlighting earthly success
questions.correctAnswer: Skill in living and practical insight, showing its superiority to strength
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'chokmah' denotes skill in living and practical insight, which Ecclesiastes 9:16 values above physical strength, underscoring wisdom’s practical importance.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:5 teaches that the dead are aware of their reward and know all things.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:5 clearly states that the dead know nothing and have no reward, emphasizing the cessation of awareness after death.

questions.question: True or False: Ecclesiastes 9:4 suggests that a living dog is better than a dead lion, symbolizing hope in life.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts a living dog with a dead lion, stating that a living dog is better, symbolizing the value of life and hope for those still living.

theological.title: Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ecclesiastes Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What theological truth is revealed in Ecclesiastes 9:1 about the relationship between human works and God's sovereignty?
options: The righteous and wise are in the hand of God, showing divine sovereignty over human works
Human works determine God's favor without His involvement
God only controls the works of the wicked
Human love and hatred are fully understood apart from God
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous and wise are in the hand of God, showing divine sovereignty over human works
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:1 teaches that the works of the righteous and wise are governed by God, emphasizing His sovereign control rather than human autonomy. This reveals God's providence over human actions.

questions.question: According to Ecclesiastes 9:2, what is the nature of death as it relates to different moral categories of people?
options: Death is the same event for the righteous, wicked, good, and unclean alike
The clean are exempt from death
Death favors the righteous over sinners
questions.correctAnswer: Death is the same event for the righteous, wicked, good, and unclean alike
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:2 states that death comes alike to all, regardless of moral distinctions, showing the universal consequence of sin and mortality.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:3 indicate about the human heart during life and after death?
options: The heart of men is full of evil and madness while alive, but after death they go to the dead without knowledge
The heart is pure and free from evil in life
After death, the heart continues to experience love and hatred
questions.correctAnswer: The heart of men is full of evil and madness while alive, but after death they go to the dead without knowledge
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the doctrine of human sinfulness and the cessation of conscious experience after death, highlighting the folly and evil present in life.

questions.question: What hope is expressed in Ecclesiastes 9:4 concerning the living compared to the dead?
options: A living dog is better than a dead lion, indicating hope in life
The dead are superior to the living
Only the strong have hope in life
The dead have more honor than the living
questions.correctAnswer: A living dog is better than a dead lion, indicating hope in life
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the value of life, even humble life, over death, emphasizing the hope and opportunity present in living.

questions.question: What doctrine about death and the afterlife is taught in Ecclesiastes 9:5?
options: The dead know nothing and have no reward, highlighting the cessation of consciousness
The dead continue to receive rewards
The living do not know they will die
The dead have full knowledge of earthly events
questions.correctAnswer: The dead know nothing and have no reward, highlighting the cessation of consciousness
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:5 teaches that the dead lack awareness and recompense, underscoring the biblical view of death as a state of unconsciousness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Ecclesiastes 9:7 where it says 'God now accepteth thy works'?
options: God's acceptance and grace toward human labor and joy
questions.correctAnswer: God's acceptance and grace toward human labor and joy
questions.explanation: The verse reveals God's gracious acceptance of human works and enjoyment, reflecting His attribute of grace and benevolence.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:10 teach about the urgency and diligence of human work?
options: Do whatsoever thy hand findeth to do with thy might because there is no work or wisdom in the grave
Work can be delayed without consequence
Work is unimportant in this life
questions.correctAnswer: Do whatsoever thy hand findeth to do with thy might because there is no work or wisdom in the grave
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the doctrine of human responsibility and the finality of death, urging diligent labor while alive.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 9:11 challenge common assumptions about human success?
options: Success is not guaranteed by swiftness, strength, wisdom, or skill but influenced by time and chance
Only the swift always win the race
Battle always goes to the strong
Riches always come to the wise
questions.correctAnswer: Success is not guaranteed by swiftness, strength, wisdom, or skill but influenced by time and chance
questions.explanation: This verse reveals the theological truth about the unpredictability of life and the sovereignty of God's providence over human ability and effort.

questions.question: What warning about human uncertainty is given in Ecclesiastes 9:12?
options: Man does not know his time of death and can be caught unexpectedly like fish or birds in a snare
Man controls his time and fate
Fishes and birds symbolize human victory
questions.correctAnswer: Man does not know his time of death and can be caught unexpectedly like fish or birds in a snare
questions.explanation: The verse teaches human ignorance regarding the timing of death, emphasizing the suddenness and certainty of mortality.

questions.question: What lesson about wisdom and human recognition is taught in Ecclesiastes 9:15-16?
options: Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is despised and his words unheard
The poor man's wisdom is always honored
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is better than strength, but the poor man's wisdom is despised and his words unheard
questions.explanation: These verses highlight the doctrinal tension between the value of wisdom over strength and the human tendency to reject humble wisdom.

questions.question: What does Ecclesiastes 9:17 teach about the influence of wise words compared to the loudness of fools?
options: Words of wise men are better heard in quiet than the cry of rulers among fools
Fools' loud cries are more effective than wisdom
Wisdom is only powerful in battle
questions.correctAnswer: Words of wise men are better heard in quiet than the cry of rulers among fools
questions.explanation: This verse teaches the enduring power and influence of wisdom over foolish authority, emphasizing the value of quiet discernment.

questions.question: How does Ecclesiastes 9:18 contrast wisdom with weapons of war, and what does it reveal about sin's destructive power?
options: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good
Weapons are more powerful than wisdom
Sin has little effect on good works
questions.correctAnswer: Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner can destroy much good
questions.explanation: This verse reveals the doctrine of sin's pervasive destructiveness despite the protective power of wisdom, emphasizing the need for righteousness.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that life is purely random with no divine order or justice. What does Ecclesiastes 9:11–12 actually teach about chance and human ignorance of time?
options: While time and chance happen to all, man does not know his appointed time, showing the limits of human control but not negating divine providence
Life is completely random without any divine oversight
Chance is an illusion and does not affect life
questions.correctAnswer: While time and chance happen to all, man does not know his appointed time, showing the limits of human control but not negating divine providence
questions.explanation: Ecclesiastes 9:11–12 acknowledges the role of chance and human ignorance about death timing, teaching humility before God's sovereign plan rather than randomness. Psalm 90:12 supports this by asking for wisdom to number our days.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about life’s value and human labor is taught by Ecclesiastes 9:4 and 9:10?
options: Life, even humble life, is valuable and work should be done with might because after death there is no work or wisdom
Life is worthless and labor is futile
Only strong people should work hard
Work and life continue after death
questions.correctAnswer: Life, even humble life, is valuable and work should be done with might because after death there is no work or wisdom
questions.explanation: Verses 9:4 and 9:10 together affirm the preciousness of life and the urgency of diligent labor, teaching the doctrine of stewardship and the finality of death.

questions.question: How do Ecclesiastes 9:6 and 9:5 together shape the biblical understanding of death’s effect on human emotions and consciousness?
options: At death, love, hatred, envy perish and the dead know nothing, indicating cessation of emotional and conscious experience
Love and hatred continue after death
The dead have eternal knowledge on earth
questions.correctAnswer: At death, love, hatred, envy perish and the dead know nothing, indicating cessation of emotional and conscious experience
questions.explanation: These verses reveal that death results in the loss of all earthly passions and awareness, teaching the doctrine of the intermediate state as unconscious rest.
